topics.title: Mass - kg and g: Compare objects using kilograms and grams; measure using scales

questions.stem: A classroom calculator has a mass of 100 grams. An equal-arm balance is used to balance the calculator with Base 10 longs (10 g each), marbles (5 g each), and chalk sticks (2 g each). How many of each unit are needed to balance the calculator?

options: Base 10 longs, because every Base 10 long has the exact same uniform mass and flat shape, whereas marbles can vary in size and chalk sticks wear down or break
Chalk sticks, because broken pieces of chalk of different lengths are the most accurate way to measure mass
Marbles, because round glass balls roll off surfaces easily and come in many different sizes
None of them, because an equal-arm balance can only compare length and not mass

steps.explain: A good informal measuring unit for mass must be **uniform** (every piece has the exact same mass) and easy to stack in the balance pan without rolling or breaking.
steps.work: \(\text{Best unit} = \text{Uniform mass and easy to handle}\)

keyPoints.note: Count the number of steps between the two clock numbers and multiply by 5 minutes for each step.

questions.solution: Moving from \(12\) to \(3\) is \(3\) number spaces of \(5\) minutes each, which takes \(3 \times 5 = 15\) minutes.

questions.stem: The minute hand counts \(60\) minutes every hour, and each number on the clock represents a span of \(5\) minutes. In e, how many minutes does it take for the minute hand to move from \(12\) to \(6\)?

questions.solution: Moving from \(12\) to \(6\) is \(6\) number spaces of \(5\) minutes each, which takes \(6 \times 5 = 30\) minutes.

questions.stem: The minute hand counts \(60\) minutes every hour, and each number on the clock represents a span of \(5\) minutes. In g, how many minutes does it take for the minute hand to move from \(4\) to \(6\)?

keyPoints.note: Count the number of steps between the two clock numbers and multiply by 5 minutes for each step.

questions.solution: Moving from \(4\) to \(6\) is \(2\) number spaces of \(5\) minutes each, which takes \(2 \times 5 = 10\) minutes.

steps.explain: Locate the starting number \(4\) and the ending number \(6\) on the clock face (highlighted in yellow).

keyPoints.note: Count the number of steps between the two clock numbers and multiply by 5 minutes for each step.

questions.solution: Moving from \(6\) to \(9\) is \(3\) number spaces of \(5\) minutes each, which takes \(3 \times 5 = 15\) minutes.

steps.explain: Locate the starting number \(6\) and the ending number \(9\) on the clock face (highlighted in yellow).

keyPoints.note: Each clock number is 5 minutes. Count 5 minutes clockwise from 12.

questions.solution: To show \(5\text{ past }12\), the minute hand must be pointing to the 1 (5 minutes past 12).

steps.explain: Read the target time on watch a: \(5\text{ past }12\) means \(5\) minutes past \(12\text{ o'clock}\).

keyPoints.note: Each clock number is 5 minutes. Count 20 minutes clockwise from 12.

questions.solution: To show \(20\text{ past }12\), the minute hand must be pointing to the 4 (20 minutes past 12).

steps.explain: Read the target time on watch c: \(20\text{ past }12\) means \(20\) minutes past \(12\text{ o'clock}\).

keyPoints.note: Each clock number is 5 minutes. Count 0 minutes clockwise from 12.

questions.solution: To show \(12\text{ o'clock}\), the minute hand must be pointing to the 12 (0 minutes past 12).

steps.explain: Read the target time on watch f: \(12\text{ o'clock}\) means \(0\) minutes past \(12\text{ o'clock}\).

questions.hint: Start at \(12\) (\(0\) minutes) and count clockwise by \(5\)s for each clock number (and by \(1\)s for individual minute marks) to reach \(22\) minutes.

keyPoints.note: Each clock number is 5 minutes. Count 22 minutes clockwise from 12.

questions.solution: To show \(22\text{ past }12\), the minute hand must be pointing 2 small minute marks past the 4 (22 minutes past 12).

steps.explain: Read the target time on watch h: \(22\text{ past }12\) means \(22\) minutes past \(12\text{ o'clock}\).

questions.stem: Look at the digital clock showing 9:23. Which written time matches this digital clock?

steps.explain: Look at the number **before the colon** (highlighted in yellow): it tells us the **hour** is \(9\).

steps.explain: Look at the number **after the colon** (highlighted in green): it tells us the **minutes past the hour** are \(23\).

steps.explain: Combine the minutes and the hour: \(23\) minutes after \(9\) o'clock is read as **23 minutes past 9**.

questions.hint: Start at 12 and skip count by 5s around the clock face (1 = 5 minutes, 2 = 10 minutes, 3 = 15 minutes, and so on) until you reach the number of minutes past the hour.

keyPoints.note: The number before "past" tells how many minutes have passed since the hour.
Divide the number of minutes by 5 (or count by 5s from 12) to find which clock number the minute hand points to.

questions.stem: The clock shows the hour hand for the time "15 past 8". Which number on the clock face should the minute hand point to so the clock shows "15 past 8"?

questions.hint: Start at 12 and skip count by 5s around the clock face (1 = 5 minutes, 2 = 10 minutes, 3 = 15 minutes, and so on) until you reach the number of minutes past the hour.

keyPoints.note: The number before "past" tells how many minutes have passed since the hour.
Divide the number of minutes by 5 (or count by 5s from 12) to find which clock number the minute hand points to.

questions.stem: The clock shows the hour hand for the time "25 past 12". Which number on the clock face should the minute hand point to so the clock shows "25 past 12"?

questions.hint: Start at 12 and skip count by 5s around the clock face (1 = 5 minutes, 2 = 10 minutes, 3 = 15 minutes, and so on) until you reach the number of minutes past the hour.

keyPoints.note: The number before "past" tells how many minutes have passed since the hour.
Divide the number of minutes by 5 (or count by 5s from 12) to find which clock number the minute hand points to.

questions.stem: Look at the analogue clock face. What time does the clock show?

steps.explain: Look at the long minute hand (red): it points straight up to 12 (0 minutes).
Look at the short hour hand (orange): it points to 12.
Put the minutes and hour together to read the clock: 12 o'clock.

questions.hint: Read the long minute hand first (3 = quarter past, 6 = half past, 9 = quarter to, or count by 5s from 12), then check the short hour hand.

keyPoints.note: Short hand shows the hour; long hand shows the minutes.

questions.stem: Look at the analogue clock face. What time does the clock show?

steps.explain: Look at the long minute hand (red): it points straight down to 6 (30 minutes = half past).
Look at the short hour hand (orange): it is halfway between 1 and 2.
Put the minutes and hour together to read the clock: Half past 1.

keyPoints.note: Short hand shows the hour; long hand shows the minutes.

questions.stem: Look at the analogue clock face. What time does the clock show?

steps.explain: Look at the long minute hand (red): it points to 4 (4 × 5 = 20 minutes past).
Look at the short hour hand (orange): it is just past 4.
Put the minutes and hour together to read the clock: 20 past 4.

keyPoints.note: Short hand shows the hour; long hand shows the minutes.

questions.stem: Look at the analogue clock face. What time does the clock show?

steps.explain: Look at the long minute hand (red): it points to 9 (15 minutes = quarter to the next hour).
Look at the short hour hand (orange): it is almost at 5.
Put the minutes and hour together to read the clock: Quarter to 5.

keyPoints.note: Short hand shows the hour; long hand shows the minutes.

questions.stem: Look at the analogue clock face. What time does the clock show?

steps.explain: Look at the long minute hand (red): it points to 5 (5 × 5 = 25 minutes past).
Look at the short hour hand (orange): it is between 11 and 12.
Put the minutes and hour together to read the clock: 25 past 11.

questions.stem: How many minutes does it take the hour hand to move from one number to the next on a clock?
questions.hint: Careful! The question asks about the hour hand, not the minute hand. Moving from one hour number to the next (for example, from \(1\) to \(2\)) is \(1\) full hour.

keyPoints.text: hour hand to move from one number to the next
keyPoints.note: The hour hand takes 1 full hour to move from one clock number to the next.

questions.solution: The hour hand moves from one number to the next in \(1\) hour, which is \(60\text{ minutes}\).

steps.explain: Read the question carefully: it asks about the hour hand (which shows hours), not the minute hand.
While the hour hand moves from one number to the next (such as from \(12\) to \(1\)), the minute hand travels all the way around the clock face once.
steps.work: \(1\text{ full turn of the minute hand} = 60\text{ minutes}\)

steps.explain: Convert \(1\) hour into minutes: \(1\text{ hour} = 60\text{ minutes}\) (whereas \(5\) minutes is for the minute hand).
Therefore, it takes the hour hand \(60\text{ minutes}\) to move from one number to the next.

questions.stem: Mrs Wilson the dentist has four morning appointments: Alana at 11:45, Bree at 10:30, Fran at 9:45, and Hilda at 11:10. What is the correct order of her appointments from earliest to latest in the morning?
